title: ablation-replace: --restore silently destroys an uncommitted edit while reporting success, and :538 hands the author the marker spelling that makes --absent pass vacuously
body:
`finding` — two defects in ONE file, surfaced by the #19348 round's `out_of_scope_findings` (report `5770753883`, PR #19640) and re-stated by the `domain:spec` seat, session `session_01UDXER3sdqfeVYpEWZs5mZx`. ⛔ Ungraded and unrouted: `domain:*`, `type` and `priority` are triage's. ⛔ Not claimed.

⚠️ **Filed as one card on purpose, and triage may split it.** Both defects live in `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` and a taker fixes them in one pass. Filing two cards would manufacture a serial collision between them on the same file. They are nonetheless **two distinct defects** and are enumerated as such below.

⚠️ Both are reported by the dev; the seat re-states them and adds its own corroboration for ①. ⛔ Neither has been independently re-measured end to end by the seat — a taker re-measures before fixing.

---

## ① `--restore` restores from HEAD, not from the pre-mutation working copy — so it destroys an uncommitted edit while printing `ok restored`

Run over a tree carrying an uncommitted edit, `--restore` writes the HEAD blob over it and then compares **only the post-restore blob** against HEAD. That comparison succeeds by construction, so it reports success having silently discarded the author's work.

Measured by the round, quoting its report: it printed `blob 4f6d6941d531 -> 22713e9104d8` going in and `blob after restore 591ef264a023` coming out, compared only the latter against HEAD, and reported success; the uncommitted edit was gone.

**Seat corroboration, first-hand and independent of the report.** At 2026-09-22T03:22Z the seat found a stray **0-byte** untracked file in the shared checkout named, literally, `22713e9104d8 going in and blob` — the middle of that very log line, mangled into a filename by the calling shell. The seat inspected it (empty, untracked, `22713e9104d8` is not a valid git object in this repo) and removed it, restoring a clean tree. ⚠️ That is evidence the run happened and that this line was printed; it is ⛔ **not** evidence about the restore logic itself, which rests on the report.

**Why it is worth fixing rather than documenting.** The ablation discipline does require committing first, which makes this a **gap rather than a contradiction** — the tool is being used the way the discipline says not to. But the failure is silent and the loss is unrecoverable, and the tool **already prints both blobs**, so comparing them to each other is roughly one line. ⚠️ A dirty tree is also exactly the state a DELETE ablation's mutate leg is in by construction (that is what #19348 is about), so the two shapes meet.

Dedupe words: `ablation-replace` · `--restore` · `restores from HEAD` · `uncommitted edit` · `ok restored`

---

## ② Line 538 prints the follow-up pre-flight command using the SOURCE anchor — the one spelling that makes `--absent` pass vacuously

`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs:538` hands the author the next command to run for a DELETE ablation, spelling the marker with the **source** anchor.

On any package whose build re-spells literals, that is precisely the spelling that makes the `--absent` **dist** reading pass **vacuously** — a marker that was never in `dist` under that spelling reads as "absent" and the ablation banks a green that measured nothing.

⭐ This is the same defect class #19348 just repaired one file over, from the other side. #19348 measured that the source spelling uses single quotes with a space after the colon while `tsup` emits double quotes with none, and that the dist and tree readings therefore demanded mutually exclusive spellings. PR #19640 gives `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` a `--source-marker` flag so the two readings stop sharing one string. **This file was never taught about it**, so it still prints the wrong half of the pair. ⚠️ So the fix is likely cheap and already designed — teach line 538 to emit `--source-marker` — but that is the taker's call after reading PR #19640, ⛔ not a prescription from here.

Dedupe words: `ablation-replace` · `line 538` · `follow-up preflight command` · `source anchor` · `vacuous absent`

---

## Consumer, and why this is not cosmetic

Every agent running an ablation. The ablation is this repo's **discriminating** measurement — it is what separates "the fix works" from "something else was green anyway". ① loses work silently; ② returns a green that measured nothing. Both corrupt the instrument the evidence discipline leans on hardest.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

- ⛔ `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` — that is #19348 / PR #19640 and is a live serial holder of that file.
- Two stale-prose items the same round noted and deliberately did not file: the `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` header names `.claude/skills/dogfood-verification/SKILL.md` as stating the script's invocation, and that file no longer mentions it; and the two documents that DO state it (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md:255`, `packages/qa/dogfood/README.md:54`) show only the default present-mode form. ⚠️ Both are `.claude/**` or doc surfaces with no behaviour attached; the round named the successor for the first as whoever lands ② (same header region) and NONE for the second.

Refs: #19348 / PR #19640 (the sibling repair and the `--source-marker` design) · #17508 (the round that first measured the re-spelling trap)
